solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Popular custom, British into beer: fine for residents!

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a habit is a custom or practice

indicators.note: one thing going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A pub-goer approves a local habit of British beer, cheering it as fine for the people who live there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' sounds like approval of the beer, but the whole phrase 'fine for residents' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitable place is one suitable to live in, so it is fit for occupants.

clue.text: Second coffee?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a moment, a very short time
second meaning: a kind of powdered coffee made by adding hot water

explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like an offer of a second cup; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment of time, and instant is also the soluble type of coffee in a jar.

clue.text: Joint within generally not wholly visible

indicators.note: something only partly visible is tucked away inside the words shown

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some joint in the body lies within and is generally not fully seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is a movable joint, as on a door or in anatomy.

clue.text: Old conspirator, very dry, on our side

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
us is our side, as against them

explanation.surface: A dry-humoured plotter of old is said to be one of ours.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the conspirators who assassinated Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Journey mostly at universal speed, leading to success

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a journey
U is the film classification for universal
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A trip taken at a steady pace ends in a happy outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement.

clue.text: Trains once operating cross part of New York

parts.note: British Rail, the former national rail operator
a machine that is on is operating
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Old trains running across a district of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran Britain's railways until privatisation in the 1990s, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronx is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: We go down, ultimately, for a very long time

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word

parts.note: the closing letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone laments that, in the end, they will be sinking for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period, an age.

clue.text: Means to travel, etc, somehow with Cyril

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cyril somehow sorts out transport and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricycle is a three-wheeled pedal vehicle, a way of getting about.

clue.text: Offend again perhaps, producing plant extract

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to sin is to offend, to transgress

explanation.surface: A repeat offence somehow results in a sticky plant product.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SIN, to sin again; 'perhaps' flags this as a playful reading of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance exuded by trees such as pines.

clue.text: Fabulous creature seen in tunic or nightgown

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted inside the following words

parts.note: the letters span the three words

explanation.surface: A mythical beast pictured on a tunic or a nightie.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a creature of fable, a horse with a single horn.

clue.text: Gas outage every so often set back big house abroad

parts.note: to gas is to chatter or talk idly

indicators.note: set back means moved backwards, so the letters are read from the end
every so often means taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A power cut now and then troubles a grand foreign mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like fuel next to 'outage', but it is the verb meaning to chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country house.

clue.text: Cause trouble with German outside team

indicators.note: outside means the first part wraps around the second

parts.note: mit is German for with
XI, Roman eleven, is a team such as a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: A German player stands outside the squad and stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With German' asks for the German word for with.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix it is an idiom for causing trouble or starting a fight.

clue.text: Brief indulgence certainly something highly valued

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a treat is an indulgence
sure! means certainly

explanation.surface: A short indulgence is surely something to prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure is a precious thing or a person much loved and esteemed.

clue.text: Fabric imposing huge weight on bed

indicators.note: on places one part after the other in an across answer

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a ton is a very large weight

explanation.surface: Some heavy material is laid on a bed and weighs it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is cloth woven from the fibres of the cotton plant.

clue.text: Capitol out of sight

indicators.note: out suggests being disordered or knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Capitol building has vanished from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of sight' reads as one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal and 'of sight' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to vision or the eyes.

clue.text: Function to take hours in place of worship

indicators.note: to take means to hold within, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
hr is the abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: A church service takes hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy site or place dedicated to worship.

clue.text: Prize money, not the first, that batsman has

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for something a batsman has, not a noun synonym

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: winnings are money won as a prize

explanation.surface: A cricketer's prize money, though not his first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a player's turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Each batsman has an innings, the spell in which they bat in cricket.

clue.text: Treatment centre using chlorine in one case primarily

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A medical centre uses chlorine, mainly in a single case.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place where patients receive medical treatment.

clue.text: Resident abroad when returning quietly stopping taxes mostly

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the result is read right to left
stopping means plugging a gap, so one part sits inside the other
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An emigrant slips home quietly to avoid most of his tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: TAXES loses its last letter, P goes between A and X, and the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, short for expatriate, lives outside their native country.

clue.text: Sauce turned up with gold rice dish

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: sauce and lip both mean cheek, insolence
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A sauce is poured over a gilded rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks culinary next to a rice dish, but here it means cheeky talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a dish of rice cooked in spiced stock.

clue.text: Stage finales for popular stories

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
finales are ends

explanation.surface: Theatre endings for well-loved tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests theatre, but it is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends are traditional tales handed down among ordinary people.

clue.text: Actress's old boast recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: An actress remembers some old bragging of hers.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a celebrated Swedish-born Hollywood film star.

clue.text: One with large bill after ruining a nice LP

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks it, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone faces a big bill after damaging a good vinyl record.
explanation.walkthrough: An LP is a long-playing record.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican is a waterbird known for its very large beak and throat pouch.

clue.text: Supplier of material for writing home

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a block of paper sheets to write on
second meaning: slang for one's flat or house

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a stationer working from home; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A writing pad provides paper, and pad is informal for a place to live.

clue.text: Method of convalescing perhaps organised by doctor

parts.note: to run something is to organise it
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A recovery plan set up by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid letters read as R AND R, rest and recuperation.
explanation.definitionFit: R and R, rest and recreation or recuperation, is one way to recover from illness.

clue.text: Large drink put out for cheat

parts.note: a double is a large measure of spirits
put out means annoyed, cross

explanation.surface: A big drink spilled for someone who swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to betray or deceive someone one is supposed to be helping.
